title: Ticket comment on ABC-123 reporting a fix
reader: The person who reported ABC-123, a support lead who does not read code and needs to know what happened and what to do next. The comment is posted on the ticket.
sources:
Ticket ABC-123 (reporter: support lead): "demo-a report export fails with a timeout when the report is large."

Dev notes (English, from the engineer):
- root cause: export ran one single DB query that loaded every row at once, no pagination. On big reports this went over the 30 s statement timeout of the database.
- fix: export now reads rows in pages of 500 and streams them into the file as it goes. Shipped in demo-a 1.4.2.
- verified on staging with a 12,000-row report: export finished without timeout.
- exports that already failed are NOT retried automatically. The reporter has to start the export again from the Reports page.
- small reports behave the same as before.

facts.text: Cause: the export loaded all rows in one query without pagination, so on large reports it exceeded the database statement timeout.
Fix: export now reads rows in pages and streams them into the file as it goes.
The fix ships in demo-a 1.4.2.
Verified on staging with a large report, which exported without a timeout.
Exports that already failed are not retried automatically; the reporter must start the export again from the Reports page.

title: Team chat message announcing a release of demo-a
reader: The demo-a team channel: developers, QA, and the support lead. They read it between other work and need to know what changed and whether they must act.
sources:
Release notes draft (mixed):
- demo-a 2.3.0 is live in production as of today 14:00 KST.
- New: CSV export on the invoice list page.
- Fixed: login redirect loop on Safari (ABC-130).
- Action needed ONLY for self-hosted installs: set the new env var EXPORT_BUCKET before upgrading, otherwise the app refuses to start. Cloud customers need to do nothing.
- Rollback: if the error rate stays above 2% for 30 minutes, the on-call engineer rolls back to 2.2.9. QA smoke test already passed on staging.

facts.text: demo-a 2.3.0 is live in production as of today 14:00 KST.
New: CSV export on the invoice list page.
Fixed: the login redirect loop on Safari (ABC-130).
Self-hosted installs must set the new env var EXPORT_BUCKET before upgrading, otherwise the app refuses to start; cloud customers need to do nothing.
Rollback: if the error rate stays above 2% for 30 minutes, the on-call engineer rolls back to 2.2.9.

title: Pull request description
reader: Two teammates who will review the pull request. They know the demo-a codebase but have not seen this change.
sources:
Task notes from the author (English):
- Problem: webhook deliveries from demo-a to customer endpoints (example.com) were dropped when the endpoint answered 503. There was no retry, so customers silently lost events.
- Change: webhook delivery now retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff, the delay doubling each time starting at 2 seconds.
- After the 5th failed attempt the event is marked `failed` and shows in the admin Events page.
- 4xx answers are NOT retried (the endpoint rejected the event on purpose).
- The max is configurable through WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES, default 5.
- Tests: unit tests for the backoff schedule, plus a manual run against a stub endpoint that returns 503 twice and then 200; the event was delivered on the third attempt.
- Reviewer focus: please check the backoff arithmetic in `backoff.py`.

facts.text: Problem: webhook deliveries were dropped when the customer endpoint answered 503, with no retry, so customers silently lost events.
Change: delivery retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff, the delay doubling from 2 seconds.
After the 5th failed attempt the event is marked failed and appears on the admin Events page.
4xx responses are not retried; the maximum is configurable with WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES (default 5).
Tested with unit tests of the backoff schedule and a manual run against a stub endpoint that failed first and then succeeded, so the event was delivered on a retry.
Reviewers should check the backoff arithmetic in backoff.py.

title: Shared document section explaining a rule
reader: New and existing developers on the demo-a team reading the team handbook. They want to know what the rule is, when it bends, and why it exists.
sources:
Handbook notes (English, from the team lead):
- Section: "Review contract for main".
- The contract: every change to the demo-a `main` branch needs one approving review from a code owner before it is merged. No self-approval.
- Exception for urgent fixes: the on-call lead can approve instead of a code owner. A code owner must then review the merged change within one business day.
- The contract applies to `main` only. Feature branches have no review requirement.
- Why: in a past incident an unreviewed change to main broke the release build and delayed the release by two days.

facts.text: Every change to demo-a main needs one approving review from a code owner before merging; no self-approval.
Urgent fixes: the on-call lead may approve instead of a code owner.
For such an urgent fix, a code owner must review the merged change within one business day.
The rule applies only to main; feature branches have no review requirement.
Reason: an unreviewed change to main once broke the release build and delayed the release.

title: Final report to a user after a change
reader: The user who asked for the change in a chat with a coding agent. They will read this one reply and decide what to do next; they have not seen the diff.
sources:
The user's request: "The nightly cleanup job in demo-a deletes files that someone is still editing. Make it skip recently modified files."

Work log (English, from the agent):
- Changed cleanup.py: the job now skips any file modified within the last 24 hours; before it deleted everything older than 7 days by creation time, which caught files edited yesterday.
- Added a regression test: a file created 10 days ago but modified 1 hour ago survives the cleanup run. The test fails on the old code and passes now. The rest of the existing test suite passes too.
- Not verified: behavior on Windows paths, no Windows machine was available here.
- Nothing is committed; the change is in the working tree.
- Open question for the user: should the same 24-hour rule apply to the tmp/ folder, which currently is cleaned separately? The agent recommends yes, to keep one rule.

facts.text: The cleanup job now skips any file modified within the last 24 hours.
Previously it deleted everything older than 7 days by creation time, which also caught files edited recently.
A new regression test checks that a file that is old by creation time but was modified recently survives the cleanup; it fails on the old code and passes now, and the existing tests still pass.
Behavior on Windows paths is not verified because no Windows machine was available.
Nothing is committed; the change is in the working tree.
Question for the user: apply the same 24-hour rule to the tmp/ folder (currently cleaned separately)? The agent recommends yes, to keep one rule.
